post.caption:
Roman harbour concrete has survived 2,000 years in seawater, while modern concrete lasts around a century. Volcanic ash in the mix reacts with seawater to grow interlocking crystals inside the material, so the sea strengthens it rather than eroding it. Recent work also suggests unblended lumps of quicklime let cracks self-heal when water reaches them. We did not lose the recipe to mystery. We optimised for speed, cost and steel reinforcement instead.
